name: Uzicko Kolo

narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

instructor.persona: A member of a local Serbian Cultural Artistic Society (KUD).
instructor.rule: counts out loud; demonstrates front and back; three slow repetitions before tempo; one correction at a time

scenes.title: Cold open
narration: Composed by accordionist Milija Spasojević in 1962, the melody of Uzicko Kolo became one of the most widespread tunes for the traditional Serbian circle dance.
This is Uzicko Kolo. 20th century.
on_screen: Hero video, first 10 seconds (Ieg8zCOmIp4)
Title card: Uzicko Kolo · Serbia · 20th century

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance is named after the town of Uzice.
Its signature melody was composed in 1962 by Milija Spasojević.
on_screen: Map: Serbia · Europe
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: A social dance performed by all social groups, ethnicities, and religious groups in Serbia.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: It is a laterally symmetrical dance performed in a closed or open circle.
The basic pattern involves moving to the right in 3 or 6 steps, followed by a mirrored sequence to the left.
Dancers maintain a bouncing motion throughout.
Watch for Triple step, Cross step.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (Ieg8zCOmIp4)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Closed or open circle, moving laterally.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is characterized by a lively melody in a major scale, often featuring a 2/4 or 3/4 time signature.
Listen for the Accordion.
The pulse is 2/4 or 3/4.
A lively, major-scale melody, typically driven by the accordion, structured in 8-measure phrases that align with the dance's lateral movement.

scenes.title: Step A — slowly
narration: Step 1: Move to the right in 3 or 6 steps.
Step 2: Perform a hopping motion in the same spot.
Footwork from the sources: 3 or 6 steps to the right, followed by 3 or 6 steps to the left, including hopping and bouncing.
Drill: Side-stepping to the right for 4 counts.
on_screen: Instructor front view, then back view (student's perspective); three repetitions
Counts on screen

scenes.title: Step B — the next layer
narration: Step 3: Move to the left in 3 or 6 steps.
Step 4: Perform a hopping motion in the same spot.
Drill: Side-stepping to the left for 4 counts.
on_screen: Instructor front and back view; slow, then half tempo

scenes.title: Put it together
narration: Step A, then Step B, without stopping. Slow first.
Now half tempo. Now full tempo.
Mirror: the instructor faces you and mirrors, so your right is your right.
Drill: Adding the bounce to the side-step.
on_screen: Split screen: front view / back view
Tempo label changes: slow → half → full
